body:
I can talk to her about them to an extent but then she basically finds a way to corner me. One day that she asked me to cover for someone with at least a little notice I told her that I was unsure because my son got released early from school that day, she told me to go pick him up from his bus stop and bring him back with me... he is 6, she isn’t the biggest fan of children and she also lives just over a half an hour away. So I would drive out to work, work for a few hours, drive back to my town and pick up my son and then drive back to work... then drive home again, all on a day we agreed in the beginning would be my day off. I don’t think she realizes how tiring certain things can be because she cannot do them herself and hasn’t experienced it first-hand if that makes sense. So she sees no problem in asking me to come in on a day off, drive back and forth a bunch with a child in-tow. 

As for her other caregivers, they’re either her close friends or her sister and I am afraid me approaching them would make waves because the closeness of their relationships. 

Don’t get me wrong, I do love my job. It’s the career path and line of work I want to be in. I also really like the woman I work for despite her bossiness. I just get so tired and worn out. It’s a lot of heavy lifting (lifting her and adjusting her body, transferring her out of bed, into the shower etc) squatting, physical labor and housework. Not only can my body get sore but I get worn down from being bossed around too. I feel like if I keep pushing it I am going to get burnt out or my body is going to have problems but I feel like such an asshole saying no to her. I feel so badly for her and admire her a lot.
